requirements.text: The rear position lamps, stop lamps, reversing lamps and rear retro-reflectors shall be so fitted that under normal conditions of use (as defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2.) and notwithstanding any vibrations to which they may be subjected, they retain the characteristics prescribed by UN R48 and enable the vehicle to comply with the requirements of UN R48.

requirements.text: For all light-signalling devices (rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp, rear retro-reflector), the reference axis of the lamp when fitted to the vehicle shall be parallel to the bearing plane of the vehicle on the road, with a tolerance of ±3°.

For the rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and rear retro-reflector (signalling devices other than side retro-reflectors and side-marker lamps), the reference axis of the lamp when fitted to the vehicle shall be parallel to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, with a tolerance of ±3°.
Any specific instructions as regards fitting laid down by the manufacturer of the lamp shall be complied with.

In the absence of specific instructions, the height and orientation of the lamps shall be verified with the vehicle unladen and placed on a flat, horizontal surface, in the condition defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2.

requirements.text: In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall be symmetrical to one another in relation to the median longitudinal plane; this requirement is not valid with regard to the interior structure of the lamp.
In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall satisfy the same colorimetric requirements.
In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall have substantially identical photometric characteristics; this shall not apply to a matched pair of a function.

If the lamp incorporates a manufacturer logo, only two lateral logos (one on each side) or one central logo can be fitted on the rear of the vehicle, and all logos that are not vehicle manufacturer or body manufacturer logos are prohibited.

The rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and rear retro-reflector may be grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated with one another provided that all requirements regarding colour, position, orientation, geometric visibility, electrical connections and other requirements, if any, are fulfilled.
The photometric and colorimetric requirements of each lamp shall be fulfilled when all other functions with which this lamp is grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated are switched OFF.

If the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with one or more other functions (e.g. the stop lamp) which can be switched ON together with it, the colour requirements of each of these other functions shall be fulfilled when the reciprocally incorporated function(s) and the rear position lamp are switched ON.

If a function is a single lamp as defined in paragraph 2.4.11.1.(a) whose apparent surface is composed of two or more distinct parts, it shall be installed such that either (a) the total area of the projection of the distinct parts of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis on a plane tangent to the exterior surface of the outer lens and perpendicular to the reference axis occupies not less than 60 per cent of the smallest quadrilateral circumscribing that projection, or (b) the minimum distance between the facing edges of two adjacent/tangential distinct parts of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis does not exceed 75 mm measured perpendicularly to the reference axis; these requirements shall not apply to a single retro-reflector.

If a function is a single lamp composed of two lamps marked "D" (paragraph 2.4.11.1.(b) or (c)), it shall be installed such that either (a) the projection of the apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis of the two lamps occupies not less than 60 per cent of the smallest quadrilateral circumscribing the projections of those apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis, or (b) the minimum distance between the facing edges of the apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis of the two lamps does not exceed 75 mm measured perpendicularly to the reference axis.
If a function is a single lamp constituted by an interdependent lamp system (paragraph 2.4.11.1.(d), marked "Y"), it shall fulfil the requirements of paragraph 5.7.2.1.

Where two or more lamps and/or two or more separate apparent surfaces are included in the same lamp body and/or have a common outer lens, these shall not be considered as an interdependent lamp system; however, a lamp in the shape of a band or strip may be part of an interdependent lamp system.

The maximum height above the ground of each lamp shall be measured from the highest point and the minimum height from the lowest point of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis; where the height clearly meets the requirements, the exact edges of the surface need not be determined.
For the purposes of reducing the geometric visibility angles, the position of a lamp with regard to height above the ground shall be measured from the H plane.

The position of each lamp as regards width shall be determined from the edge of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis furthest from the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle when referred to the overall width, and from the inner edges of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis when referred to the distance between lamps; where the position clearly meets the requirements, the exact edges need not be determined.

In the absence of specific instructions, the photometric characteristics (e.g. intensity, colour, apparent surface) of the rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp shall not be intentionally varied during the period when the lamp is switched ON.

The photometric characteristics of the lamp may vary (a) in relation to the ambient light, (b) as a consequence of other lamps being switched ON or OFF, or (c) when the lamp is being used to provide another lighting function, provided that any variation is in compliance with the technical provisions for the lamp concerned.
Red light emitted by the rear position lamp, stop lamp and rear retro-reflector fitted on the rear of the vehicle shall not be visible from the front of the vehicle.

There shall be no direct visibility of the apparent surface of a red lamp (rear position lamp, stop lamp) if viewed by an observer moving within Zone 1 in a transverse plane situated 25 m in front of the vehicle (see Annex 4).

requirements.text: In case of doubt, the requirement of no visibility of red light towards the front shall be deemed fulfilled if the luminous intensity of the red light emitted to the front, as verified during type approval of the lamps, is not more than 0.25 cd per lamp, taking into account the influence of the vehicle body if applicable.

requirements.text: The electrical connections shall be such that the rear position lamps can only be switched ON and OFF simultaneously with the front position lamps, the end-outline marker lamps and side-marker lamps (if they exist) and the rear registration plate lamp; this does not apply while front and rear position lamps are switched ON as parking lamps, side-marker lamps flash with direction indicators, daytime running lamps are switched ON, or the front position lamp function is substituted under paragraph 5.12.1.
If the lamp is part of an interdependent lamp system, all light sources of the system shall be switched ON and OFF simultaneously.
Where a closed-circuit tell-tale is prescribed (e.g. for the position lamps), it may be replaced by an "operating" tell-tale.

Concealment of the rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and rear retro-reflector shall be prohibited (concealment is only permitted for main-beam headlamps, dipped-beam headlamps and front fog lamps).
The colour of the light emitted by the reversing lamp shall be white.
The colour of the light emitted by the stop lamp shall be red.
The colour of the light emitted by the rear position lamp shall be red.
The colour of the rear retro-reflector, non-triangular, shall be red.
The number of rear position lamps, stop lamps, reversing lamps and rear retro-reflectors mounted on the vehicle shall be equal to the number indicated in the individual specifications of UN R48.
With the exception of retro-reflectors, a lamp, even bearing an approval mark, is deemed not to be present when it cannot be made to operate by the sole installation of a light source and/or a fuse.

If the rear position lamp (category R2) and stop lamp (category S2) have variable luminous intensity control responding to the conditions of paragraphs 5.26.1. and 5.26.2., the intensity of these lamps, when combined, grouped or reciprocally incorporated, shall vary all together in the same manner and in a similar proportion.

If the rear position lamp (category R2) and stop lamp (category S2) have variable luminous intensity control, the specific prescribed ratio between the luminous intensities of the two lamps, if applicable, shall be maintained over the entire intensity range throughout variation transitions.

If the rear position lamp (R2) and stop lamp (S2) have variable luminous intensity control, an increase and decrease of luminous intensity, within the limits prescribed in the pertinent UN Regulations, is allowed in relation to ambient lighting, fog, snowfall, rain, spray, dust clouds and contamination of the light emitting surface.

If the rear position lamp (R2) and stop lamp (S2) have variable luminous intensity control, a decrease of luminous intensity, within the limits prescribed in the pertinent UN Regulations, is allowed independently of environmental conditions as long as the vehicle speed is equal to or less than 20 km/h or the distance to the following vehicle is equal to or less than 20 m; an already activated decrease may remain active as long as the vehicle speed is equal to or less than 50 km/h.
If the rear position lamp and stop lamp have variable luminous intensity, no sharp variation of intensity shall be observed during transition.
If the rear position lamp and stop lamp have variable luminous intensity, it may be possible for the driver to set these functions to static luminous intensities.

When the vehicle electrical system is in a constant voltage operating condition, the voltage supplied at the terminals of the stop lamp and rear position lamp, where according to their type-approval documentation they were tested with a special power supply/electronic light source control gear, in a secondary operating mode or at a voltage requested by the applicant, shall not exceed the voltage specified for those devices or functions as approved; this does not apply to devices which include an electronic light source control gear or a variable intensity control as part of the device.

In all other power supply conditions, with the vehicle electrical system in a constant voltage operating condition, the voltage at the terminals of the stop lamp and rear position lamp shall not exceed 6.75 V (6 V systems), 13.5 V (12 V systems) or 28 V (24 V systems) by more than 3 per cent; this does not apply to devices which include an electronic light source control gear or a variable intensity control as part of the device.
The means of controlling the maximum voltage at the terminals of the stop lamp and rear position lamp may be located within the body of the device.

There shall be no obstacle on the inside of the angles of geometric visibility to the propagation of light from any part of the apparent surface of the lamp observed from infinity; however, no account is taken of obstacles already present when the lamp was type-approved.

If, when the lamp is installed, any part of its apparent surface is hidden by further parts of the vehicle, proof shall be furnished that the part of the lamp not hidden by obstacles still conforms to the photometric values prescribed for the approval of the device.

When the vertical angle of geometric visibility below the horizontal may be reduced to 5° (lamp at less than 750 mm above the ground measured from the H plane), the photometric field of measurements of the installed optical unit may be reduced to 5° below the horizontal.
If the lamp is part of an interdependent lamp system, the geometric visibility requirements shall be fulfilled when all its interdependent lamps are operated together.
The LED modules do not need to be replaceable, if so stated in the communication sheet of the component type approval.

The rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and rear retro-reflector shall be type approved according to the corresponding device Regulations as specified in the relevant subparagraphs of paragraph 6 of UN R48 when installed on a vehicle.
If the light-signalling lamp incorporates a manufacturer logo, the lamp shall be type approved according to the requirements of UN Regulation No. 148.

A device type approved according to any preceding series of amendments to UN Regulations Nos. 148 and/or 150 is deemed equivalent to one approved according to the latest series of amendments when the change indexes related to each individual lamp (function) do not differ, and may then be fitted on the vehicle without any update of the device type approval documents and device markings.
A reversing lamp is mandatory on motor vehicles (including category M1).
On motor vehicles of category M1, one reversing lamp device is mandatory and a second reversing lamp device is optional.
Reversing lamp devices shall be type-approved according to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 23, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.
The reversing lamp shall be positioned in height not less than 250 mm and not more than 1,200 mm above the ground.
The reversing lamp shall be positioned in length at the rear of the vehicle.
The geometric visibility of a reversing lamp installed at the rear of the vehicle, defined by angle α as specified in paragraph 2.10.7., shall be α = 15° upwards and 5° downwards.

The geometric visibility of a reversing lamp installed at the rear of the vehicle, defined by angle β as specified in paragraph 2.10.7., shall be β = 45° to the right and to the left if there is only one device, and 45° outwards and 30° inwards if there are two devices.
The reversing lamp shall be oriented rearwards.

The electrical connections of the reversing lamp shall be such that the lamp can be switched ON only if the reverse gear is engaged and if the device which controls the starting and stopping of the propulsion system is in such a position that operation of the propulsion system is possible.

The reversing lamp shall not switch ON or remain ON if either the reverse gear is not engaged or the device which controls the starting and stopping of the propulsion system is not in a position where operation of the propulsion system is possible.
A tell-tale for the reversing lamp is optional; however, a tell-tale indicating failure is mandatory if required by the component regulation.
Stop lamp devices of S1 or S2 categories are mandatory on all categories of vehicles, including M1.
Two stop lamp devices of S1 or S2 category shall be installed on the vehicle.
The stop lamp devices shall be type-approved according to the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 7, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.

Stop lamp position in width (M1 and N1 vehicles): for S1 or S2 category devices, the point on the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle; there is no special requirement for the distance between the inner edges of the apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axes.

Stop lamp position in height for S1 or S2 category devices: above the ground, not less than 350 mm nor more than 1,500 mm (2,100 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm and if the optional lamps are not installed).
Stop lamp position in length for S1 or S2 category devices: at the rear of the vehicle.

Stop lamp geometric visibility, horizontal angle for S1 or S2 category devices: 45° to the left and to the right of the longitudinal axis of the vehicle; however, for S1 and S2 stop lamps mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.

Stop lamp geometric visibility, vertical angle for S1 or S2 category devices: 15° above and below the horizontal; however, where the lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.
Stop lamp orientation: towards the rear of the vehicle.
All stop lamps shall be switched ON simultaneously when the braking system provides the relevant signal defined in UN Regulations Nos. 13 and 13-H.
The stop lamps need not function if the device which starts and/or stops the propulsion system is in a position that makes it impossible for the propulsion system to operate.
Stop lamp tell-tale is optional; however, a tell-tale indicating failure is mandatory if required by the component regulation.
Rear position lamp devices of R or R1 or R2 categories are mandatory.
Two rear position lamps shall be installed on the vehicle.
The rear position lamps shall be type-approved according to the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 7, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.

Rear position lamp position in width: the point on the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle; for M1 and N1 vehicles there is no special requirement for the distance between the inner edges of the two apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axes.

Rear position lamp position in height: above the ground, not less than 350 mm nor more than 1,500 mm (2,100 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm and if the optional lamps are not installed).
Rear position lamp position in length: at the rear of the vehicle.

Rear position lamp geometric visibility, horizontal angle: 45° inwards and 80° outwards; however, where the lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.

Rear position lamp geometric visibility, vertical angle: 15° above and below the horizontal; however, where the lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.

For M1 and N1 vehicles, as an alternative to paragraph 6.10.5.1., at the manufacturer's discretion and only if a rear side-marker lamp is installed on the vehicle, the rear position lamp horizontal geometric visibility angle may be 45° outwards to 45° inwards; where the lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.

For M1 and N1 vehicles using the alternative geometric visibility of paragraph 6.10.5.2. (only if a rear side-marker lamp is installed), the rear position lamp vertical angle shall be 15° above and below the horizontal; where the lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.

When the alternative geometric visibility of paragraph 6.10.5.2. is used, the rear position lamp, to be considered visible, shall provide an unobstructed view of the apparent surface of at least 12.5 cm²; the illuminating surface area of any retro-reflector that does not transmit light shall be excluded.
Rear position lamp orientation: rearwards.
Rear position lamp electrical connections shall be in accordance with paragraph 5.11.

requirements.text: A closed-circuit tell-tale is mandatory for the rear position lamps; this requirement does not apply when daytime running lamps are switched ON.
The rear position lamp tell-tale shall be combined with that of the front position lamps.
A tell-tale indicating failure of the rear position lamps is mandatory if required by the component Regulation.
Rear retro-reflectors, non-triangular, are mandatory on motor vehicles.
Two rear non-triangular retro-reflectors shall be installed on the vehicle.

The rear non-triangular retro-reflectors shall be type-approved according to the requirements concerning Class IA or IB retro-reflectors in the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 3, or in the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 150.

Rear non-triangular retro-reflector position in width: the point on the illuminating surface which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle; for M1 and N1 vehicles there is no special requirement for the distance between the inner edges of the two apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axes.

Rear non-triangular retro-reflector position in height: above the ground, not less than 250 mm nor more than 900 mm (not more than 1,200 mm if grouped with any rear lamp(s); 1,500 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 900 mm or 1,200 mm respectively).
Rear non-triangular retro-reflector position in length: at the rear of the vehicle.
Rear non-triangular retro-reflector geometric visibility, horizontal angle: 30° inwards and outwards.

Rear non-triangular retro-reflector geometric visibility, vertical angle: 10° above and below the horizontal; however, where the retro-reflector is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward angle of 10° may be reduced to 5°.
Rear non-triangular retro-reflector orientation: rearwards.
The illuminating surface of the rear non-triangular retro-reflector may have parts in common with the apparent surface of any other lamp situated at the rear.

When the daytime running lamps are switched ON, the rear position lamps shall be switched ON. However, the rear position lamps may be switched OFF when the daytime running lamps are switched ON, and may remain switched OFF as long as the ambient light conditions outside the vehicle are above 7,000 lux (measured according to the requirements of Annex 13).

requirements.text: In conformity of production checks, the angles of geometric visibility of the rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and rear retro-reflector, checked according to paragraph 2.10.7., shall fulfil the individual specifications applicable to each lamp; the angle limits may have an allowance corresponding to the ±3° variation permitted in paragraph 5.3. for the mounting of light-signalling devices.

When the electrical connections are checked by switching on every lamp supplied by the vehicle electrical system, the rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp and their tell-tales shall function in accordance with paragraphs 5.11. to 5.14. and the individual specifications applicable to each lamp.

The presence, number, colour, arrangement and, where applicable, category of the rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and rear retro-reflector, checked by visual inspection of the lamps and their markings, shall fulfil paragraphs 5.15. and 5.16. and the individual specifications applicable to each lamp.
